editorial.headline: The open quarrying code Bali can still register
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 08109 covers residual stone, sand, and clay extraction, with national foreign ownership open up to 100% and no Bali moratorium block at large scale.
editorial.body:
KBLI 08109 is the residual home for extraction businesses working with stone, sand, and clay that sit outside the more narrowly named extraction buckets. In practical terms, it reaches quarrying and digging for materials such as diorite, basalt, and breccia, as well as dredging sedimentary material from the sea. The scope is not limited to taking material from the ground or seabed: it also includes the immediate handling that makes the material commercially usable, such as breaking, crushing, separating, screening, and smoothing.

That makes this a production-facing activity rather than a purely trading or brokerage label. A founder using it should be describing an operation connected to physical extraction and first-stage processing of these materials. The slim record also ties the activity to exploration-stage mining business licences for certain non-metal minerals and for rocks. Those references matter because they signal the sectoral character of the code: this is an extractive activity with mineral and rock licensing context, not a general construction-supply category dressed up as one.

The scale picture is unusually broad. The record opens the code to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar businesses, so it can serve anything from a very small domestic operation to a large-scale enterprise, provided the registered activity is genuinely within the extraction and processing scope. Nationally, it is also marked TERBUKA for PMA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. Put plainly, the national investment list does not cap foreign ownership below full control for this activity.

The Bali reading is the important point. The province’s moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island, permanently, but this record is not blocked: its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and the stated reason is that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. So the honest conclusion is not that Bali is closed to this foreign-owned quarrying activity today. On this slim record, a PMA can register it in Bali, while still needing to treat the activity as a higher-risk extractive operation rather than a light administrative registration.
